messages:
matt: kicking off a routing safety scan for the new LHR-gpu2 cluster. scope: transit peering, TGW routing, NAT/egress capacity, private DNS, plus a fast k8s/gpu smoke so handoff isn't premature. planning to run checks in this thread and tag who signs off.

sophie: scope clear. are we doing any slow path tests (eg large-batch infer) or just connectivity/egress + quick endpoint check?

matt: mostly connectivity + egress + node/gpu readiness. one tiny inference (10–20 tokens) to validate model endpoint and auth plumbing.

ari: PASTE RUNBOOK CHECKLIST BELOW -- follow in order and paste results as you go.

ari: STEP 1 - Transit & peering verification
- AWS: verify TGW attachments: `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=vpc-id,Values=vpc-lhr-gpu2` -> expect AttachmentState = available and ResourceType = vpc
- check TGW route table propagation: `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-route-tables --filters Name=transit-gateway-id,Values=tgw-0123456789` -> find propagated entries for the region CIDRs
- confirm no blackhole routes: look for `State` != `blackhole` in `describe-route-tables` outputs for TGW-associated routes
- if partner BGP present: validate BGP adjacency is Established on the partner appliance and that `local-pref` is sane

kevin: note from last bring-up: propagation can be disabled by default on new TGW RTs. verify `transitGatewayRouteTable.Propagations` and ensure the VPC association has `State=associated`.

matt: STEP 2 - Local route tables & subnet default routes
- run: `aws ec2 describe-route-tables --filters Name=association.vpc-id,Values=vpc-lhr-gpu2` and `--query 'RouteTables[*].Routes'` to inspect 0.0.0.0/0 and TGW entries
- ensure private subnets point to `nat-` or TGW attachment as intended, not accidentally to an IGW
- check for overlapping customer CIDRs that could prefer local attachment (use `ip route` tooling or spreadsheet)

ana: costs/ops question: are we using managed NAT gateways for this cluster or a shared NAT instance pool? managed NAT is simpler but high-per-hour cost for bursty jobs.

matt: default for this region is managed NAT. infra budget flagged this morning — please include estimated EIP count and expected GB egress in handoff notes.

oncall-bot: Reminder: NAT gateways incur hourly and per-GB charges. See /ops/nat-gateway-costs and tag billing for region approvals.

sophie: STEP 3 - Egress smoke & metrics
- from an ephemeral pod in `dev` namespace: `kubectl run netcheck --image=radial/busyboxplus:curl -i --restart=Never --rm --command -- sh -c \"curl -sS http://ifconfig.me && sleep 1\"` -> verify returned EIP is one of expected NAT EIPs
- traceroute to S3 endpoint: `traceroute -n s3.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com` -> verify path traverses TGW or NAT depending on routing design
- CloudWatch quick check: query NATGateway `BytesOut` and `ActiveConnections` for last 24h, look for spikes/503s. example insights: `FIELDS @timestamp, bytes, metricName | FILTER metricName = \"BytesOut\"`

ari: STEP 4 - Private DNS & zone associations
- confirm private hosted zone association: `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-lhr-gpu2` -> hosted zone id present and correct environment tag
- from inside cluster pod: `dig +short internal-service.lhr.private` should return internal IPs; if NXDOMAIN or public IP, stop and investigate split-horizon config
- validate Route 53 resolver rules if using inbound/outbound endpoints for cross-region lookups

kevin: STEP 5 - k8s node & GPU basic health
- `kubectl get nodes -l accelerator=nvidia -o wide` -> expected count (e.g., 8) and Ready status
- `kubectl describe node <gpu-node>` -> confirm `Capacity` shows gpu resources and `Conditions` has Ready=True, Kernel+Kubelet not in crashloop
- check nvidia-device-plugin logs on one node: `kubectl -n kube-system logs daemonset/nvidia-device-plugin-daemonset` for allocation errors

kevin: STEP 6 - endpoint smoke test (tiny inference)
- exec from pod with internal network access: `curl -sS -X POST https://internal-model.lhr/api/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}'` -> expect 200 and short text
- if 403/401: validate VPC endpoint/ALB auth and security group rules between cluster and model service

ari: STEP 7 - observable & SLO checks before handoff
- ensure per-route dashboards show expected latency percentiles for last 1h (p50/p95) and no recent error budget burn
- add a Grafana snapshot link with CPU/GPU utilization during tests and NAT gateways bytes metrics

matt: once all checks pass, assign handoff to `infra-oncall` with: list of verified items, NAT EIPs, hosted zone id, node counts, and a short note on cost sensitivity. include `next-run` window for a rerun after 24–48h of traffic.

ana: I'll prepare the cost snippet and expected monthly egress for the ticket.

oncall-bot: Scheduled runbook reminder set for +24h to re-evaluate NAT load.

matt: tagging @sophie @kevin for signoff. please paste one-line ACK after you finish your verification steps.

sophie: ACK - TGW propagation confirmed, private DNS OK, egress IPs look correct.

kevin: ACK - nodes 8/8 Ready, device plugin healthy, tiny inference returned 200. no blackholes found.

matt: thanks all — handing off to infra-oncall now. attaching a short checklist to the ticket.
